examples.question_text: Write $\sec\alpha$, $\operatorname{cosec}\alpha$ and $\cot\alpha$ in terms of the primary trigonometric functions, stating when each reciprocal expression is valid.
examples.solution_text:
$\sec\alpha=\dfrac{1}{\cos\alpha}$ when $\cos\alpha\ne0$.

$\operatorname{cosec}\alpha=\dfrac{1}{\sin\alpha}$ when $\sin\alpha\ne0$.

$\cot\alpha=\dfrac{1}{\tan\alpha}$ when tangent is defined and nonzero, so both $\sin\alpha\ne0$ and $\cos\alpha\ne0$.

The definition $\cot\alpha=\dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}$ also applies when $\cos\alpha=0$, provided $\sin\alpha\ne0$.

Relative to $\alpha$, the opposite side is $6$, the adjacent side is $8$ and the hypotenuse is $10$.

$\begin{align*}\operatorname{cosec}\alpha&=\dfrac{\text{hyp}}{\text{opp}}\\&=\dfrac{10}{6}\\&=\dfrac53\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\sec\alpha&=\dfrac{\text{hyp}}{\text{adj}}\\&=\dfrac{10}{8}\\&=\dfrac54\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\cot\alpha&=\dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{opp}}\\&=\dfrac86\\&=\dfrac43\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
Find the requested exact reciprocal ratio in each right-angled triangle.

(a) Relative to acute angle $\theta$, the hypotenuse is $26$ and the adjacent side is $10$. Find $\operatorname{cosec}\theta$.

(b) Relative to acute angle $\beta$, the opposite side is $9$ and the adjacent side is $40$. Find $\sec\beta$.

Without using a calculator, find the exact values of:

(a) $\sec150^\circ$

(b) $\operatorname{cosec}225^\circ$

(c) $\cot\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The reference angle is $30^\circ$. Cosine is negative in quadrant II.

$\cos150^\circ=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$\begin{align*}\sec150^\circ&=\dfrac{1}{\cos150^\circ}\\&=-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\\&=-\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{3}\end{align*}$

(b) The reference angle is $45^\circ$. Sine is negative in quadrant III.

$\sin225^\circ=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$.

$\begin{align*}\operatorname{cosec}225^\circ&=\dfrac{1}{\sin225^\circ}\\&=-\sqrt2\end{align*}$

(c) The reference angle is $\dfrac\pi3$. Tangent is negative in quadrant IV.

$\tan\dfrac{5\pi}{3}=-\sqrt3$.

$\begin{align*}\cot\dfrac{5\pi}{3}&=\dfrac{1}{\tan(5\pi/3)}\\&=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\\&=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{3}\end{align*}$

Add one full turn to find an angle with the same terminal arm.

$-\dfrac\pi3+2\pi=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.

The reference angle is $\dfrac\pi3$. Tangent is negative in quadrant IV, so $\tan\dfrac{5\pi}{3}=-\sqrt3$.

$\begin{align*}\cot\left(-\dfrac\pi3\right)&=\cot\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\\&=\dfrac{1}{\tan(5\pi/3)}\\&=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\\&=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{3}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Secant requires cos(alpha) nonzero; cosecant requires sin(alpha) nonzero. The reciprocal-tangent expression requires both sine and cosine nonzero. Cotangent itself equals cos(alpha)/sin(alpha), so it remains defined and equals zero when cosine is zero and sine is nonzero. This matches the supplied accepted domain clarification.

The diagram places alpha opposite side 6 and adjacent to side 8, with hypotenuse 10; 6²+8²=10². Cosecant=10/6=5/3, secant=10/8=5/4 and cotangent=8/6=4/3. The triangle faithfully adapts the supplied worked example.

For (a), opposite=√(26²−10²)=√576=24, giving cosecant=26/24=13/12. The solution diagram has consistent side proportions and angle placement. For (b), hypotenuse=√(9²+40²)=√1681=41, giving secant=41/40. Both missing-side cases use the source's Pythagoras-then-ratio method.
Cos150°=−√3/2, so sec150°=−2/√3=−2√3/3. Sin225°=−1/√2, so cosec225°=−√2. Tan(5π/3)=−√3, so cot(5π/3)=−1/√3=−√3/3. Reference angles and quadrant signs agree with the source's exact-ratio exercises.

−π/3+2π=5π/3 gives the same terminal arm. Its reference angle is π/3 in quadrant IV, where tangent is −√3. Therefore cot(−π/3)=−1/√3=−√3/3. Equivalent-angle reduction and reciprocal evaluation match the mapped assessed method.

The unit-circle diagram correctly marks (0,1), (1,0) and (0,−1). At 270°, x=0 makes secant undefined. At 360°, y=0 makes cosecant undefined. At π/2, cotangent=x/y=0/1=0 despite tangent being undefined. At zero, y=0 makes cotangent undefined. These conclusions follow the source boundary table and coordinate diagram.
